title: Condensed coefficient rings $\underline T$
statement:
The *pro-étale site of a point*, $*_{\mathrm{proét}}$, is the category of profinite sets
with the coherent topology. In it, a finite family $\{S_i\to S\}$ covers $S$ exactly when
$\coprod_iS_i\to S$ is surjective, and a sieve covers when it contains such a family. A
*condensed ring* is a sheaf of rings on $*_{\mathrm{proét}}$. By [sk-def-sfb-ring-object],
its underlying condensed abelian group is a ring object of $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$.

For a topological ring $T$, the condensed ring $\underline T$ is defined by its sections,

$$
\underline T(S):=C(S,T),
$$

with restriction by precomposition and pointwise ring operations. It is a sheaf, and its
underlying ring object of $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ is commutative when $T$ is. A
continuous ring homomorphism $\varphi\colon T\to T'$ induces a morphism of condensed rings
$\varphi_*\colon\underline T\to\underline{T'}$ by postcomposition, and this is functorial in
$\varphi$.

Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with the absolute
value extending that of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. This gives the following commutative condensed
rings:

- $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell$ and $\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, for the $\ell$-adic topologies;
- for a subfield $E$ of $\Qlb$ (a field with an embedding $E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$), the
  condensed rings $\underline E$ and $\underline{\cO}_E$. Here $E$ has the topology
  restricted from $\Qlb$, and $\cO_E=\{x\in E:|x|\le1\}$ is its ring of integers.

Postcomposition with continuous inclusions gives the morphisms of condensed rings
$\underline{\cO}_E\to\underline E$, and, when $E$ contains $\mathbf Q_\ell$ compatibly with
the embedding, $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\to\underline E$ and
$\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\cO}_E\to\underline E$.

proof.text: The displayed finite jointly surjective covering families specify the site used throughout this definition; a condensed ring means a sheaf of rings on this site. For an arbitrary topological ring $T$, [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] gives precisely the presheaf $S\mapsto C(S,T)$ with precomposition restrictions and pointwise operations, together with its sheaf property. Its underlying abelian sheaf has a ring object structure, commutative if $T$ is commutative, by the same cited statement. For a general sheaf of rings on this site, clause 3 of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] supplies the asserted ring object of abelian sheaves. This uses no completeness or finiteness hypothesis on $T$.

source.place: First two sentences: sheaf property and ring object structure

proof.text: For a continuous ring homomorphism $\varphi:T\to T\prime$, [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] supplies the sheaf morphism with section map $a\mapsto\varphi\circ a$, its morphism of underlying ring objects, and both functoriality identities. Its section formula commutes with restriction because $\varphi\circ(a\circ u)=(\varphi\circ a)\circ u$. The identity and composition formulas are evaluated on each section as $\mathrm{id}\circ a=a$ and $(\psi\circ\varphi)\circ a=\psi\circ(\varphi\circ a)$.

For the fixed prime $\ell$, [def-sfb-padic-int-condensed-ring] and [def-sfb-padic-condensed-ring] specify $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell(S)=C(S,\mathbf Z_\ell)$ and $\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(S)=C(S,\mathbf Q_\ell)$ for the $\ell$-adic topologies. Both cited statements assert commutativity of their underlying ring objects. The latter also supplies $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ by the sectionwise inclusion.

source.place: Sentence on the four instances: the two standard padic rings

proof.text: For an arbitrary field embedding $E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$, [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring] specifies the restricted topology and $\underline E(S)=C(S,E)$. With that topology, [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring] specifies the valuation subring $\cO_E=\{x:|x|_E\le1\}$, its subspace topology, and $\underline{\cO}_E(S)=C(S,\cO_E)$. Both cited statements assert commutativity of the underlying ring objects. The latter supplies the map $\underline{\cO}_E\to\underline E$ without assuming that $E$ contains $\mathbf Q_\ell$.

source.place: Sentence on the four instances: the embedded subfield and its integers

proof.text: Assume now, exactly as in the final clause, that $E$ contains $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and the embedding in $\Qlb$ is compatible with it. The conditional clause of [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring] supplies $\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\to\underline E$, and that of [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring] supplies $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\cO}_E$. Combine these with $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ from [def-sfb-padic-condensed-ring] and $\underline{\cO}_E\to\underline E$ from [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring] to obtain the two displayed chains. Every arrow is the postcomposition map for its underlying inclusion. Thus on a section $a:S\to\mathbf Z_\ell$ each composite sends $s$ to the image of $a(s)$ in $E$; the two composites agree. The functoriality identity of [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] expresses this equality as equality of condensed ring morphisms.
